title: Jointly continuous homogeneous coordinate linear equivalence
statement:
Let $E$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a topology making addition, multiplication and inversion on $E\setminus\{0\}$ continuous. Let $J$ be a group with a topology making multiplication and inversion continuous. Let $V$ be an $E$-vector space with a topology making addition and scalar multiplication continuous, and with an $E$-linear $J$-action for which $J\times V\to V$ is continuous. For $n\geq0$ let $B_J^n(V)$ be the space of jointly continuous functions $F:J^{n+1}\to V$ with $F(ax_0,\ldots,ax_n)=aF(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$, and let $C_J^n(V)$ be the space of continuous functions $J^n\to V$, with $C_J^0(V)=V$. All finite powers have the product topology, and both spaces have pointwise operations. Write $P_n(g_1,\ldots,g_n)=(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_n)$ and $r_n(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=(x_0^{-1}x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}^{-1}x_n)$. Put $\Phi_{J,n}F=F\circ P_n$ and $(\Psi_{J,n}f)(x)=x_0f(r_n(x))$, using empty tuples for $n=0$. The spaces $B_J^n(V)$ and $C_J^n(V)$ are $E$-vector subspaces of their respective spaces of all functions. For every $n\geq0$ the formulas define mutually inverse $E$-linear maps $\Phi_{J,n}:B_J^n(V)\to C_J^n(V)$ and $\Psi_{J,n}:C_J^n(V)\to B_J^n(V)$: in particular $\Psi_{J,n}f$ is jointly continuous and equivariant, and $\Phi_{J,n}F$ is continuous. Explicitly,
$$\Phi_{J,n}\Psi_{J,n}=\operatorname{id}_{C_J^n(V)},\qquad \Psi_{J,n}\Phi_{J,n}=\operatorname{id}_{B_J^n(V)}.$$
In degree zero these maps are $F\mapsto F(1)$ and $v\mapsto(x\mapsto xv)$. No compactness, Hausdorffness or discreteness assumption is made. This assertion concerns graded vector spaces only.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-initial-topology-continuity] with the coordinate projections: the product topology is the coarsest topology making those projections continuous, since its basic open rectangles are finite intersections of their inverse images of opens. Thus a map into a finite product is continuous exactly when each coordinate is continuous, including the empty product. Composites of continuous maps are continuous because $(v\circ u)^{-1}(O)=u^{-1}(v^{-1}(O))$. Constant maps are continuous because their inverse images of opens are empty or the whole domain. In subsequent steps, pairing continuous maps and composing with an assumed continuous operation therefore preserves continuity.

source.place: Tag 08ZS, section-limits, opening product-topology description (lines 2342–2350); initial-topology criterion supplied by lem-weil-pbc-initial-topology-continuity. Elementary preimage calculations are agent-written.

proof.text: The zero function is continuous. For continuous functions $f,h$ on the same domain and $c\in E$, the maps $f+h$ and $cf$ are continuous by pairing $f,h$ (respectively the constant $c$ and $f$) and composing with the given continuous addition (respectively scalar multiplication). Thus the continuous functions form an $E$-vector subspace: closure under negatives follows from $-f=(-1)f$, and the vector-space identities hold pointwise over the field [def-weil-field]. If $F,H$ are equivariant, then $(F+H)(ax)=aF(x)+aH(x)=a(F+H)(x)$ and $(cF)(ax)=c(aF(x))=a(cF(x))$, since the $J$-action is $E$-linear; zero is equivariant as well. This proves the two subspace assertions. In degree zero identify functions on the singleton $J^0$ with their values in $V$.

proof.text: For $n\geq1$, set $p_0(g)=1$ and $p_{i+1}(g)=p_i(g)g_{i+1}$ for $0\leq i<n$. The base $p_0$ is continuous. If $p_i$ is continuous, then $(p_i,g_{i+1})$ is continuous into $J\times J$, and composition with multiplication proves that $p_{i+1}$ is continuous. Induction proves continuity of every coordinate of $P_n=(p_0,\ldots,p_n)$; the product criterion proves continuity of $P_n$. For $n=0$, $P_0$ is the constant tuple $(1)$ and is continuous. Hence $\Phi_{J,n}F=F\circ P_n$ is continuous for every $F\in B_J^n(V)$.

proof.text: For $1\leq i\leq n$, the coordinate $x\mapsto x_{i-1}^{-1}x_i$ is continuous: compose the $(i-1)$st projection with inversion, pair with the $i$th projection, and compose with multiplication. The product criterion gives continuity of $r_n$; for $n=0$ it is the unique map to a singleton. Consequently $f\circ r_n$ is continuous. Pair it with the continuous projection $x\mapsto x_0$ and compose with the assumed jointly continuous action $J\times V\to V$. This proves joint continuity of $\Psi_{J,n}f$ for every $n$, using the singleton interpretation of $f\in C_J^0(V)=V$.

proof.text: For $a\in J$, each ratio satisfies $(ax_{i-1})^{-1}(ax_i)=x_{i-1}^{-1}a^{-1}ax_i=x_{i-1}^{-1}x_i$. Therefore $r_n(ax)=r_n(x)$ and $(\Psi_{J,n}f)(ax)=(ax_0)f(r_n(x))=a(x_0f(r_n(x)))$, also when $n=0$. Thus $\Psi_{J,n}f$ is equivariant. Evaluation gives $\Phi(F+H)=\Phi(F)+\Phi(H)$ and $\Phi(cF)=c\Phi(F)$. Linearity of the action gives $\Psi(f+h)(x)=\Psi(f)(x)+\Psi(h)(x)$ and $\Psi(cf)(x)=c\Psi(f)(x)$. These identities and the preceding continuity checks make both arrows well-defined $E$-linear maps.

proof.text: For $g=(g_1,\ldots,g_n)$, the first coordinate of $P_n(g)$ is $1$. Since $p_i=p_{i-1}g_i$, its successive ratios are $p_{i-1}^{-1}p_i=g_i$ for $1\leq i\leq n$. Hence $r_n(P_n(g))=g$, and $(\Phi_{J,n}\Psi_{J,n}f)(g)=1f(g)=f(g)$. For $n=0$ this reads $(\Psi_{J,0}v)(1)=1v=v$. Equality at every input proves $\Phi_{J,n}\Psi_{J,n}=\operatorname{id}$.

proof.text: For $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$, induction gives $p_i(r_n(x))=x_0^{-1}x_i$ for $0\leq i\leq n$: at $i=0$ both sides are $1$; the next step is $(x_0^{-1}x_i)(x_i^{-1}x_{i+1})=x_0^{-1}x_{i+1}$. Thus $P_n(r_n(x))=x_0^{-1}x$ coordinatewise. Equivariance gives $(\Psi_{J,n}\Phi_{J,n}F)(x)=x_0F(x_0^{-1}x)=x_0(x_0^{-1}F(x))=F(x)$. Equality at every input proves $\Psi_{J,n}\Phi_{J,n}=\operatorname{id}$. This uses only associativity and cancellation, so $J$ need not be abelian.

proof.text: In degree zero the definitions give $\Phi_{J,0}F=F(1)$ and $\Psi_{J,0}v=(x\mapsto xv)$, and equivariance gives $F(x)=xF(1)$. The two inverse identities and linearity above therefore hold in every stated degree and give the asserted graded vector-space equivalence. All continuity arguments use only the product topology and the continuous operations in the hypotheses, so no separation, compactness or discreteness hypothesis is required.
